elements.element: The liability cap applies to both parties on a mutual, equivalent-scope basis.
elements.evidence: Although both parties have the same numerical formula, Contractor's cap covers only liability relating to performance of services under a Statement of Work, while Company's cap covers any liability arising out of the Agreement.

elements.element: The cap amount is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Both capping sentences use the greater of the stated 12-month paid-or-payable fees measure and USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded for both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 7(b) initially excludes indirect damages mutually, but the later statement that the 'foregoing limitations' do not apply to Excluded Claims also disables this exclusion for those claims.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded for both parties.

result.reason: The operative language includes the requested cap formula and all listed carve-outs, but the base cap is not fully mutual because the parties' covered claim scopes differ. More importantly, stating that the 'foregoing limitations' do not apply to Excluded Claims reaches both the cap and the indirect/consequential-damages exclusion, contrary to the stated intent to make those claims merely uncapped while leaving Section 7(b) intact. The duplicated payment language is unnecessary and 'all amounts due' is broader than the requested Customer-payment treatment; 'Customer' is also inconsistent with the defined party label 'Company.' The fallback amount is not met because the USD 1,000,000 floor remains.
